question: DEF Lotus 4v5, contact confirmed on C Site, you are Killjoy at B Site. How do you rotate to C as fast as possible given the rotating doors?

options.label: Open the B-C rotating door and rotate through it to reach C faster, accepting the sound cue it creates
options.explication_courte: On Lotus, the B-C rotating door shortens the rotation: arriving at the right site in time is worth more than the audio cue the door opening creates.

options.label: Rotate through the standard path (CT Corridor) to avoid giving the ATK any audio warning of your rotation
options.explication_courte: The standard CT path is silent and avoids telegraphing your rotation, but it is longer; on a confirmed C contact, speed to site may outweigh the stealth.

sources_option.citation: Silent standard rotations avoid the door audio cue but are slower; on a confirmed hit, arriving late through the quiet path can mean reaching the site after the plant.

options.label: Stay at B Site and hold your position in case the C contact is a fake
options.explication_courte: Holding B on a confirmed C contact leaves your teammates outnumbered on the real site: in a 4v5 you cannot afford to anchor a site that may be a fake.

sources_option.citation: Lotus rewards fast rotations across its three sites; anchoring a site with no confirmed contact while teammates are outnumbered elsewhere wastes a defender.

options.label: Open the B-C door but wait the full 10s for it to finish rotating before stepping through
options.explication_courte: Waiting the full 10-second door rotation cycle defeats the entire speed advantage: the door offers a passable gap DURING rotation, not only after it is open.

sources_option.citation: Rotating doors give a small passage window during the 10-second spin; waiting for the door to fully finish rotating negates the speed benefit entirely.

explication_longue:
Situation: DEF Lotus 4v5, contact CONFIRMED on C Site, you are Killjoy at B Site. The question is how to reach C as fast as possible.

Lotus is the three-site map with fast rotations via its two unique rotating doors. The B-C door is a shortcut that cuts the B-to-C rotation time significantly. On a CONFIRMED contact (not a fake), speed to the right site is the priority: the audio cue of opening the door is a known Lotus mechanic that experienced players account for, but arriving in time to help defenders outweighs the warning.

The standard CT Corridor path (acceptable) is completely silent and avoids revealing your rotation, but it is notably longer and may be too slow on a confirmed call. Staying at B on a confirmed C hit (costly) leaves teammates in a numbers deficit at the real site. Opening the door but waiting 10 seconds for it to fully rotate (mistake) destroys the speed advantage - you can pass through during the rotation.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% open B-C door and rotate through, ~23% CT Corridor silent rotation, ~16% hold B on fake read (costly), ~5% open and wait 10s (mistake).

sources.citation: Both rotating doors take exactly 10 seconds to fully rotate; rotating doors help speed up defensive rotations — being at the right site faster is worth more than silent rotations that arrive too late.
Lotus has two doors that make rotations faster from A to B or B to C, helping you decide and execute site defenses faster across the three sites.
Rotating doors announce movement with an audio cue but provide fast rotations; the door gives a passage window during its 10-second spin, not only after.
